methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik, a Series C autonomous transportation company, is evaluated against a comp universe of 8 private frontier-tech peers in Transportation—including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia—with no public comparables available. The company has raised $356M to date across its funding rounds.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable to this valuation. Using total capital raised ($356M) as a proxy for post-money valuation, and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage progression, the implied valuation reaches $605M. A peer-median approach is not applicable; while three same-sector companies exist, insufficient narrow-filter matches (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) preclude robust triangulation—requiring three or more comparable datapoints to avoid misleading conclusions.

The single-method analysis supports a valuation range of $514M to $695M, with a median point of $605M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.7x multiplier for Gatik's specific market position within autonomous freight, the timing and structure of a potential Series D, and the valuation trajectory of comparable private peers. Without public market reference points or tighter peer clustering, refinement of this range would require additional proprietary diligence on current round terms and company-specific traction metrics.
